title: Summarise a memory map
description:
A memory tool receives a list of regions from a `VirtualQuery` walk and has to present them compactly. Write two functions.

`merge(regions)` combines **neighbouring** regions that have the same state, protection and type into one: a region is a neighbour of the previous one when it starts exactly where the previous one ends. The input is sorted by address. Regions that are not touching, or that differ in any attribute, stay separate.

`totals(regions)` returns how many bytes are committed, how many reserved and how many free.

```
{ 0x1000, 0x1000, COMMIT, rw, PRIVATE }
{ 0x2000, 0x2000, COMMIT, rw, PRIVATE }    -> merged with the one before: { 0x1000, 0x3000, ... }
{ 0x4000, 0x1000, COMMIT, r,  PRIVATE }    -> different protection: separate
{ 0x6000, 0x1000, COMMIT, r,  PRIVATE }    -> not touching (gap at 0x5000): separate
```
hints: Build the output as you go. For each region, look at the last region already in the output: if it ends exactly where this one starts and every attribute matches, grow it by this region's size instead of adding a new one.
"Ends exactly where this one starts" is `last.base + last.size == r.base`.
lessonTitle: Exploring Your Own Process with VirtualQuery
